title: Full mock — senior-style round
exp: Thirty minutes, mixed format. Score on reasoning clarity, trade-off commitment, and use of real examples. Generic answers score low; real project examples score high.
pts: **System design (15 min):** "Design a compliance alert notification service — triggers when a control goes out of compliance"
**Debugging (10 min):** "A SCIM batch job completes but some users aren't being provisioned. No errors in logs. Walk through your investigation"
**Behavioral (5 min):** "Tell me about a technical decision you'd make differently today"
**Scoring:** 1pt = stated the problem clearly, 1pt = named trade-offs explicitly, 1pt = used a real example or concrete implementation detail

viz.note: After the mock, ask your AI for a strengths-vs-gaps summary so you know exactly what to revisit before the real interview.

qa.q: Sample: Design the compliance alert notification system.
qa.a: Requirements: alert when control status → non-compliant, deliver via email/Slack, at-least-once delivery, no duplicate alerts for same issue. Architecture: Status Change → DB event/app event → Message Queue (Azure Service Bus) → Alert Worker (checks dedup in Redis by alert key + TTL) → Notification Service (SendGrid + Slack webhook). Key decisions: queue for at-least-once delivery; Redis dedup to prevent spam; notification history table for audit trail.

qa.q: Sample: SCIM batch job completes silently but users aren't provisioned.
qa.a: 1) Check batch job logs — is it logging success per user? If yes: issue is downstream. 2) Check IdP response — are SCIM calls returning 2xx? 3) Add request/response logging if missing. 4) Check downstream system logs — is it receiving provisioning events? 5) Check for silent filter — user attribute check silently skipping users who don't match a condition. 6) Trace one specific user manually — follow the data. This is a "data not flowing" problem.

qa.q: Sample: A technical decision you'd make differently today.
qa.a: (Use a real one.) Example: "On the BMS migration, I did a big-bang cutover rather than a strangler-fig pattern due to schedule pressure. It led to a 48-hour stabilisation period. Today I'd advocate harder for phased rollout — the extra time is almost always less than incident response time if something goes wrong in a big-bang cutover."
